text:
mike: Heads-up — GPU fleet hit sustained 92% util in us-west-2 for last 8m, queue depth spiking. We need a short-term admission change tied to real capacity instead of static key caps.
anya: ugh. any impact on prod traffic? metrics? :grimacing:
ops-bot: alert: gpu_utilization(us-west-2) = 92.3% over 8m; pending_queue = 312; avg_latency_token_ms = 2200
mike: Not yet customer-facing errors, but tail latency is creeping and we're approaching load-shed thresholds. Proposal: replace single static token-bucket per api_key with a two-tier credit system: 1) fast local leaky-window for burst credit; 2) shared reservoir per org that refills proportionally to available headroom on the fleet/region.
simon: interesting. So refill rate = f(available_gpus, free_slots) rather than fixed tokens/sec? That avoids over-commit on hot regions.
neha: important: we must preserve paid-tier burst guarantees and avoid punting free-tier to zero. budgeting + billing signals needed if we throttle.
mike: yes — idea is: each region reports a headroom factor H in [0,1]. credit_refill = base_refill * H * tier_multiplier. burst tokens come from local bucket up to bucket_size. Once burst exhausted, admission is gated by org reservoir.
anya: can you sketch the admission pseudocode? makes it easier for infra to implement today.
simon: pasted quick sketch:
```\n# per-request admit
H = get_region_headroom(region)
refill = base_refill * H * tier_multiplier(org)
api_key_bucket.refill(refill)
if api_key_bucket.consume(1):
    allow()
elif org_reservoir.consume(1):
    allow()
else:
    enqueue_or_reject()
``` 
mike: we also need a slow-moving feedback loop to avoid oscillation — e.g., 30s smoothing on H, and a separate cool-down if we see repeated enqueue/reject flaps.
neha: what about fairness across orgs when H is low? priority weights or min-guarantees?
james: suggestion: preserve a tiny emergency quota per org (min_q), and offer a best-effort pool that is weighted by recent spend + SLA tier. also consider soft-fallback to cheaper model variant for non-critical requests.
anya: operational concerns: how do we surface this in console? customers need to see headroom and predicted throttle probability.
mike: agree — add telemetry: region_headroom, org_reservoir_level, key_bucket_level; expose via /metrics and console panel. will add eval events when a request hits org_reservoir to track user-visible regressions.
eeps-bot: deploy-check: make sure rollout is toggleable per-region and has canary percent.
simon: implementation note: don't store reservoir state in a single db if we need low-latency — use in-memory with durable snapshots and fallback to Redis for cross-node sync.
neha: cost note: if we shift more requests to cheaper models as fallback, we reduce GPU pressure but may shift to CPU inference costs — need cost calculator in rollout.
mike: OK action items: 1) eng-infra to prototype headroom endpoint + smoothed H (simon, mike) 2) eng-runtime to add two-tier admission API (anya, james) 3) product/console to wire telemetry and UI (neha) 4) run canary in us-west-2 at 10% traffic and monitor 1h. I'll open a RFC doc and a canary runbook.
anya: ok will start a branch for runtime hooks, pinging simon for headroom API contract.
simon: will stub headroom endpoint today.
mike: thanks — syncing tomorrow after initial canary metrics. :thumbsup:
